title: Fact vs Dimension Tables, Cardinality & Star Schema Design
summary: Separate quantitative Facts from descriptive Dimensions cleanly, eliminate flat single-table bloat, and prevent ambiguous bi-directional loops.
learningObjectives: Distinguish narrow additive numeric Fact tables from wide descriptive Dimension lookups
Enforce single-direction `One-to-Many (Dimension -> Fact)` filtering preventing circular ambiguity
prerequisiteConcepts: Normalized SQL / Power Query cleaned tables

sections.heading: 1. Why VertiPaq Loves Clean Star Schemas
sections.content:
Analysts coming from Excel often jam 80 product, customer, store, and numeric sales columns into ONE giant flat table! While tiny files work fine, flattening duplicates text labels millions of times, slows slicers, and breaks multi-fact comparisons (e.g., comparing Monthly Budgets vs Daily Sales cleanly!).

A **Star Schema** keeps **Fact Tables** tall and numeric (foreign keys + numeric measurements like `Quantity`, `Revenue`, `Discount`) surrounded by **Dimension Tables** (`DimProduct`, `DimCustomer`, `DimDate`) filtering cleanly **Downhill** in **One-to-Many single direction** (`1 -> *`). Avoid toggling 'Both' bi-directional cross-filtering globally—it triggers subtle ambiguity loops and severely hurts query performance!

codeExamples.explanation: Dimensions slice downwards into central numeric Fact tables in crisp Star geometry.

keyPoints: Hide foreign key columns (`ProductKey`, `CustomerKey`) inside Fact tables from Report View so report builders slice cleanly strictly from Dimension fields!
Drop unused high-cardinality millisecond timestamps or transaction UUID columns unless drilled directly into visuals.
commonMistakes: Turning every relationship to 'Bi-directional' just to filter a slicer count instead of using clean DAX `CROSSFILTER` inside one measure.

sections.heading: 2. Handling Multiple Fact Tables Safely
sections.content: Compare how conformed dimensions (`DimDate`, `DimRegion`) safely cross-slice both `FactSales` and `FactTargets` simultaneously without ever joining Fact-to-Fact directly.

codeExamples.code:
// Variance vs Target works seamlessly because BOTH facts hang off conformed DimDate & DimRegion!
Actual Revenue = SUM(FactSales[Revenue])
Target Revenue = SUM(FactTargets[TargetAmount])
Target Variance % = DIVIDE([Actual Revenue] - [Target Revenue], [Target Revenue])
codeExamples.explanation: Sharing conformed Dimensions slices unrelated Fact tables smoothly without risky Fact-to-Fact joins.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Accurate side-by-side matrix comparing Actual vs Target across Regions and Months

keyPoints: Keep relationships clean: 1 -> * single direction from conformed Dimensions to each Fact table.
commonMistakes: Linking `FactSales` directly to `FactTargets` via Many-to-Many links (producing doubled/corrupt aggregates!).

exercises.title: Refactor Multi-Fact Flat Model Into a Star Schema
exercises.objective: Separate descriptive attributes from quantitative facts cleanly.
exercises.description: You have `RawSales(OrderID, Date, StoreName, StoreManager, ProductSKU, Category, Qty, Price)` and `StoreBudgets(Month, StoreName, BudgetAmt)`. Design the clean Star Schema relationships.
instructions: Identify the 3 Dimension tables and 2 Fact tables.
List exact cardinality (`1:*`) and filter direction arrows.
Explain how Store slicers affect BOTH Revenue and Budget seamlessly.

exercises.solutionExplanation: Conformed `DimStore` and `DimDate` sit above `FactSales` and `FactBudgets` with clean `1 -> *` single-direction filters.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why does hiding Fact-table foreign key IDs (e.g., `FactSales[CustomerID]`) improve report usability and accuracy?

options.text: Prevents accidental slicing by incomplete transaction keys instead of clean complete attributes inside `DimCustomer`
Deletes foreign key data from disk freeing 50% RAM

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Users should slice strictly by Dimension attributes while aggregating Fact measures.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why should indiscriminate bi-directional (`Both`) relationship filtering across multiple Fact tables be avoided?

options.text: Creates ambiguous circular filter paths that fail deployment and slow VertiPaq queries down significantly
Removes numeric decimals from currency measures
Prevents exporting PBIX files to PDF

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Single-directional Star filters keep semantic behavior crisp and unambiguous.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: In a well-tuned Star Schema comparing Sales against Budgets, how are `FactSales` and `FactBudgets` connected?

options.text: Both are filtered cleanly downwards (`1 -> *`) by shared conformed Dimensions like `DimDate` and `DimStore` without directly joining Fact-to-Fact
Linked directly via a Many-to-Many bridge without Dimensions
Merged sideways into a single duplicated row table
Left disconnected and unified using visual text overlays

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Conformed Dimensions synchronize filtering across disparate granularities safely.

recap: You designed clean VertiPaq Star Schemas preventing flat bloat, Fact-to-Fact mistakes, and bi-directional ambiguity.
